to.fees: $5/vehicle day-use e-Pass or $30 annual Northwest Forest Pass, purchasable via Recreation.gov
to.rules: Leave No Trace; no camping within 0.25 mile of Blue Lake; no stock or mechanized travel on the climbers' path
to.permit: No climbing or wilderness permit required
to.closures: SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) is gated and closed for winter, typically early-to-mid December through mid-April/May depending on snowpack
to.seasonal: WA-20 (North Cascades Highway) closes gate-to-gate roughly early December–mid/late April; the entire Washington Pass corridor is car-inaccessible in winter.
to.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District
to.land_manager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
to.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
to.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency (America the Beautiful) Pass

overnight_permit.where: This is general Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest land outside any wilderness boundary; parties bivy informally at the trailhead or a highway pullout. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is needed to park, and no camping is allowed within a quarter mile of Blue Lake itself.

wa_south_early_winters_spire_nothing.notes: Checked as asked: MP states 5.11d A0, Sport/Aid/Alpine, 1000 ft (303 m), 12 pitches, Grade III, FA Ron Cotman and Leland Windham, July 2001; the stored grade, pitches, length and FA all match. Pitches 12 matches the only published topo (P1-P12 graded on MP). The route is nearly all bolted (MP gives per-pitch bolt counts; P8 5.4 has no protection) and MP's protection line is 20 quickdraws; no total bolt count is stated, so bolts not proposed (a sum would be derived). FA not locked (MP only; an FA never locks at the 1-source tier). theCrag sent my tab to its bot check on the second area page, so no second source could be read; grade, pitches and length are at the 1-source tier. MP's spire page recommends the SR-20 hairpin for routes on the EAST side; this route is on the south/southeast slabs reached from the South Arete base, so Blue Lake is its trailhead.

wa_north_early_winter_spire_constantino_.notes: SETTLED which spire: SOUTH Early Winter Spire. The 1979 AAJ report written by David Whitelaw (AAJ vol. 22) places the Constantino-Whitelaw line on the southeast face of South Early Winter Spire: begun 1976, finished in one day in July 1977 with Duane Constantino; second ascent solo by Quin Koenig. So area_id (wa_south_early_winters_spire) is right and the ID is wrong: CATALOG DEFECT, the id says NORTH (not moved or renamed). Free grade F9 agrees with the stored 5.9 but is one source, not locked. No pitch total or length is given (four leads to a ledge, then several more). FA added from the first-ascent party's own AAJ report, unconfirmed (an FA never locks on one source). The route is not on Mountain Project's spire page; theCrag blocked my tab.
